query: For a CoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy matrix evaluated in sliding from room temperature to 800 °C, what single intervention could overcome the difficulty of maintaining low coefficient of friction and wear rate throughout the full temperature range? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains the mechanism expected to operate across the test regime, predicts performance relative to the starting CoCrFeNi material, specifies relevant temperature, load, and environmental boundaries, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes a controlled falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a small silver phase into a CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy (HEA) will enable an adaptive Ag-rich tribofilm and compacted oxide glaze to form under sliding, thereby maintaining a lower coefficient of friction and wear rate from room temperature to 800 °C relative to the baseline CoCrFeNi.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic CoCrFeNi HEA (single-phase FCC), fine-grained (≤20 µm), polished to Ra ≤ 0.05 µm, no intentional solid-lubricant phase.
generation.intervention: Add 5–15 at% Ag to CoCrFeNi to create a dual-phase HEA–Ag composite in which Ag segregates to grain boundaries and can enrich the surface under shear (e.g., via vacuum arc melting or powder metallurgy followed by homogenization to achieve Ag-rich discrete regions).
generation.conditions: Unlubricated pin-on-disk sliding in dry air (20–50% RH) against an inert ceramic counterface (Al2O3), normal load 5–10 N, sliding speed 0.05–0.2 m/s, temperatures stepped at ~25, 200, 400, 600, and 800 °C; ambient pressure.
generation.structural_mediator: A continuous or quasi-continuous Ag-rich tribofilm co-deposited and compacted on the wear track together with a mixed, fine-grained oxide glaze (Cr- and Co-containing spinels and chromia) stabilized by the soft Ag phase; Ag present along grain boundaries and near-surface regions acting as a shear-accommodating third body.
generation.mechanism: At low temperatures, Ag’s low shear strength and ductility allow it to smear and accommodate interfacial shear, reducing junction growth and adhesive/abrasive interactions. As temperature increases, tribo-oxidation of Co/Cr/Fe/Ni generates mixed oxides; the Ag phase promotes compaction, continuity, and healing of the oxide glaze, suppressing third-body abrasion and maintaining a low-shear interface. Ag’s high thermal stability (melting point ~962 °C) and limited oxidation in air support film persistence up to 800 °C.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to baseline CoCrFeNi, the Ag-containing composite will exhibit a lower and more stable coefficient of friction across 25–800 °C (approximately 20–50% reduction, with the largest reduction above ~500 °C) and a reduced specific wear rate (roughly 2–5× lower at ≥600 °C and 1.5–3× lower at ≤400 °C), with smoother, continuous tribofilms observed on the wear tracks.
generation.baseline: Unmodified CoCrFeNi HEA under the same test conditions, expected to show increasing friction and wear with temperature due to oxidative/abrasive wear and discontinuous oxide debris without a ductile, lubricious carrier phase.
generation.boundary: Benefits are expected in oxidizing or mildly humid air with inert ceramic counterfaces (Al2O3, Si3N4), for loads up to ~20 N and speeds up to ~0.3 m/s. Performance may degrade in high vacuum (limited oxide formation), under very high contact pressures causing Ag squeeze-out or depletion, or against reactive metallic counterfaces at high temperature where interdiffusion or chemical reactions could disrupt film continuity.
generation.uncertainty: No direct prior evidence is provided here for CoCrFeNi–Ag across this exact temperature span; the magnitude of friction/wear reductions and film continuity at 800 °C depend on Ag distribution, phase stability, and counterface interactions. Ag coarsening or depletion during prolonged high-temperature sliding could limit effectiveness.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two materials: (i) equiatomic CoCrFeNi and (ii) CoCrFeNi–10 at% Ag with similar grain size and surface finish. Confirm Ag forms a discrete, segregated phase (SEM/EDS, XRD). Conduct pin-on-disk tests in dry air against Al2O3 at 25, 200, 400, 600, and 800 °C, load 10 N, speed 0.1 m/s, sliding distance 500 m per temperature. After each test, analyze wear tracks and counterface for tribofilm composition and continuity.
measurements: Steady-state coefficient of friction at each temperature
Specific wear rate (volume loss per unit load and distance) of the HEA sample
SEM/EDS mapping of wear track for Ag distribution and oxide phases
XPS or Raman spectroscopy of tribofilm chemistry (Ag presence, spinel/chromia content)
Cross-sectional FIB-TEM of wear track to assess film thickness and continuity
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if (a) the Ag-containing material does not reduce the coefficient of friction by ≥20% compared to baseline at ≥3 of the 5 temperatures, or (b) the specific wear rate is not lower at ≥3 temperatures, or (c) no Ag-enriched tribofilm (and associated compacted oxide glaze) is detected on the wear track at ≥600 °C.
